doc.title: Putter Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 27, 2024

title: Studying with Herman Reinshagen and harmony classes
summary: Smith began serious study at 16 with Herman Reinshagen, who taught Mingus and Jimmy Bond, using the Simandl book. He also had years of school harmony classes and the Hindemith text.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: So from that point did you feel it was necessary to start taking lessons? To expand not only your playing of the bass but your understanding of how music works?

Oh yes. Yes. I began studying seriously when I was 16 with the same guy that taught Charlie Mingus and there was a bass player named Jimmy Bond here, and all of the guys studied with this man, whose name is Herman Reinshagen, and the book at that time was the Simandl book, that was the bass study book and that was put together by a guy named Fred Zimmermann. And in the introduction Fred Zimmermann talks about how he was Reinshagen’s prize pupil and like that. And so it was really a great privilege to have

studied with Herman. I’ve studied with, sometimes I say 20 people maybe. Maybe — more than ten people I have studied with. And in school at that time, in high school, junior high and high they had harmony classes, which were the study of, actual study of voice leading. And there were usually about eight people in the class and I had that for about five years and so I was studying and writing stuff and there was one profound book by Paul Hindemith called Traditional Harmony. So I attribute my knowledge of the interior of harmony and voice leading and all that stuff from that, and then the other technique, and then I played as much as possible. You know I was obsessive like one needs to be.
